{{Short description|Mathematical Lemma}}
{{distinguish|Cartan's theorem (disambiguation){{!}}Cartan's theorem|Cartan's lemma}}
In [[potential theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], '''Cartan's lemma''', named after [[Henri Cartan]], is a bound on the measure and complexity of the set on which a logarithmic [[Newtonian potential]] is small.

==Statement of the lemma==
The following statement can be found in Levin's book.<ref>B.Ya. Levin, ''Lectures on Entire Functions''</ref>

Let ''&mu;'' be a finite positive [[Borel measure]] on the complex plane '''C''' with ''&mu;''('''C''')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''n''.  Let ''u''(''z'') be the logarithmic potential of&nbsp;''&mu;'':

:<math>u(z) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_\mathbf{C} \log|z-\zeta|\,d\mu(\zeta)</math>

Given ''H''&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;(0,&nbsp;1), there exist discs of radii ''r''<sub>''i''</sub> such that

:<math>\sum_i r_i < 5H</math>

and

:<math>u(z) \ge \frac{n}{2\pi}\log \frac{H}{e}</math>

for all ''z'' outside the union of these discs.
